design.user_group: Exactly one of visual, hearing, motor, cognitive. It is duplicated in task JSON for self-contained analysis even though the directory also encodes the group.
design.subgroup_ids: One or more broad, non-mutually-exclusive functional/population subgroups. These are intentionally coarse and should not be treated as diagnoses or prevalence categories. A user group may have only one broad subgroup when the benchmark tasks do not support a meaningful finer split.
design.need_ids: One or more finer-grained documented accessibility needs from documented_user_need_taxonomy.json.
design.relationship: During benchmark curation, subgroup_ids are assigned consistently from need_ids using need_id_to_subgroup_ids. This is a metadata construction rule, not a runtime inference requirement; a task may belong to multiple subgroups when the broad groups genuinely overlap.

V-S1.name: Blindness
V-S1.definition: Tasks relevant to users who require non-visual access to interface/content or alternatives to visual-only information and verification.

V-S2.name: Low vision / visual perception difficulty
V-S2.definition: Tasks relevant to users who benefit from magnification, contrast/palette/color support, or assistance perceiving visual content.

H-S1.name: Deaf or hard of hearing
H-S1.definition: Tasks relevant to users who need or benefit from non-auditory access to speech, alerts, media, verification, or other sound-dependent information.

M-S1.name: Keyboard input difficulty
M-S1.definition: Tasks relevant to users who have difficulty using a physical keyboard or simultaneous modifier-key input.

M-S2.name: Pointer / fine-motor control difficulty
M-S2.definition: Tasks relevant to users who have difficulty with conventional pointing, dragging, target precision, mouse-button use, or sustained fine-motor control.

M-S3.name: Involuntary input / timing difficulty
M-S3.definition: Tasks relevant to users affected by accidental/repeated input or tightly timed input demands.

C-S1.name: Attention / information-processing difficulty
C-S1.definition: Tasks relevant to users who benefit from reduced distraction, simplification, prioritization, or help extracting important information.

C-S2.name: Memory / time-management difficulty
C-S2.definition: Tasks relevant to users who benefit from external memory support, reminders, time cues, or reduced short-term retention burden.

C-S3.name: Executive function / decision-making difficulty
C-S3.definition: Tasks relevant to users who benefit from planning, sequencing, task-state tracking, choice support, or error prevention.

C-S4.name: Numerical / reconciliation difficulty
C-S4.definition: Tasks relevant to users who benefit from assistance with calculation, counting, copying, or reconciling information across sources.
